- If key == 'X_train': f_index = ['gbr', 'gbr_gs', 'rfr', 'rfr_gs'] (4 elements)
- Else: f_index = ['gbr2', 'rfr2'] (2 elements)

For `'X_train'`:

- rfr was trained on X_train

- gbr2 was trained on X_2_train
- rfr2 was trained on X_2_train

Specifically, X_2_train contains only the transformed2 columns while X_train has all the one-hot encoded features, so their arrays naturally differ in dimension. The model assignments are reversed. When iterating over 'X_train', the code uses X_train.columns, but gbr_gs and rfr_gs trained on X_2_train have fewer features (8) compared to X_train's larger feature set (108). This mismatch in feature counts prevents proper array stacking.

The solution is to reorganize model_dict so that models trained on the same dataset are grouped together. I should place gbr_gs and rfr_gs under 'X_2_train' and keep only gbr and rfr under 'X_train'.
